responsibility: Immutable, explicitly supplied access-context facts: scope, membership, strength, surface, actor.
non_responsibilities: Authentication: verifying passwords, tokens, sessions or multi-factor challenges.
Authorization: capabilities, grants, policies, ownership, decisions and denials.
Membership lookup, site selection, disabled-user handling and any read of live or stored state.
Building a context from an HTTP request, a session store, a container or ambient global state.
The closed set of trusted system identities and the authority each one carries.
Persistence, transport, host-schema serialization and container registration.

capabilities.title: Site, organization and workspace scope values
capabilities.description: Normalised, bounded scope identifiers as three distinct types that never convert or compare.

capabilities.title: Versioned membership snapshot
capabilities.description: Server-resolved organization and workspace membership with versions, fingerprinted to fail stale.

capabilities.title: Principal and system-actor contracts
capabilities.description: Host-implemented contracts through which a context sees a human principal or an explicit system actor.

capabilities.title: Authentication strength, surface and step-up proof
capabilities.description: Closed strength and surface vocabularies with an ordering, and the bound fifteen-minute step-up proof.

capabilities.title: Execution context
capabilities.description: The immutable per-unit-of-work envelope a host mints once and supplies explicitly to every use case.

capabilities.title: Typed refusal
capabilities.description: The one InvalidArgumentException subclass every refusal raises; it names the rule, never the input.
